headline: A bitmask remembers used elements; a remainder remembers the current bucket
statement: Decide whether every element of nums can be assigned to exactly k nonempty groups with identical sums. Values are positive and group order does not matter.
constraints: Each value appears at most four times.
intuition: Each group must sum to total divided by k. Use a bit mask to record which input positions are already used, and save the sum in the current unfinished group. Add an unused number only if it fits. Reaching the group target starts a fresh group.
approach: Reject totals not divisible by k, or any value larger than target.
Set remainder[0]=0 and all other masks unreachable.
For every reachable mask, add an unused element only if it fits the current group.
Store the resulting sum modulo target; accept if the full mask is reachable.
correctness: A reachable mask represents completed target-sum groups plus one unfinished group whose sum is its stored remainder. Adding a fitting unused value maintains this invariant, and reaching target completes a group. Every legal partition can be built group by group through these transitions. Since all values are positive, groups are nonempty; the full total equals k*target, so a reachable full mask completes exactly k groups.
bruteForce: Assign each element to one of k labeled buckets, giving up to k^n combinations. Bitmask DP merges equivalent used-element states.

complexity.explanation: At most 2^n masks each inspect n unused positions.

pitfalls: Divisibility alone does not prove a partition exists.
Do not reuse an element whose bit is already set.
Zero remainder means a completed bucket; reset by modulo only after fitting the target.
